name: Diyarbakır
summary_text: Route-3 estimate, now carrying real sub-national evidence: the south-east's largest metropolis, with a conflict-era security legacy (state-of-emergency legacies, village-guard system, high police presence). On 14 September 2024 - the day of a national anti-LGBT "Great Family Gathering" - two men attacked two trans women with sharp objects in the Kayapınar district: Sudenaz Uran was killed at the scene and her friend was injured; the defendants recorded the killing and the recording entered the case file. On 19 December 2025 both were sentenced to aggravated life imprisonment for intentional killing of a woman - the strongest homicide-justice outcome in this country's record - though during the trial the Family and Social Services Ministry's application to intervene was accepted while the local bar association's LGBTI+ commission's was rejected, casting the state as guardian of "the family" rather than of the victim's community. Scored relative to the national score (0.15) for Turkey.

sources.title: Türkiye: Draft Law Threatens LGBT People with Prison | Human Rights Watch
sources.claim_summary: Human Rights news release (29 October 2025): the leaked 11th Judicial Package omnibus draft law would amend the penal and civil codes to criminalise conduct deemed "contrary to biological sex and general morality" (up to three years), sharply restrict gender-affirming healthcare (minimum age 25, onerous eligibility conditions) and allow criminal charges against both trans people and the professionals providing their care; the government's stated justification is protecting "the family" and "public morals"; the package also carries unrelated measures such as longer child sentences and online-content removal.

Kaos GL's LGBTI+ Human Rights Report 2025, "The Year of the Family: A Major Siege Against LGBTI+ People" (published 24 February 2026): finds that in 2025 anti-LGBTI+ hostility became explicit state policy — centred on the presidency, with the family ministry as the implementing ministry, religious and broadcasting authorities deployed against LGBTI+ people, and the closure of an LGBTI+ rights organisation within this structure.

sources.title: İstanbul police detain trans women for ID checks amid profiling concerns
sources.claim_summary: NOTE: page not retrievable at fetch time (JS-rendered page; only site navigation in the cache); the underlying bianet report (31 July 2025) covers around 20 trans women rounded up in the Beyoğlu district during ordinary activity — street, shopping, cafés — taken to a police station for identity checks, held about two hours with their names recorded and videos filmed, no official reason given; one detainee: "this is profiling".
